label: prf:skein-polynomial-transfer-matrix
title: Proof of skein polynomial transfer matrix
html:
Proof. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_A(q) is defined over the ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Each crossing factor C_{ij} = c_j \sigma_i + d_j has coefficients (c_j, d_j) in \mathbb{Z}[\tfrac12][q^{\pm 1}] (the factor \tfrac12 enters only through the mixed crossing):

Pair type c_j d_j Hecke element
\mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p} 1 0 \sigma
\mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n} 1 -(q - q^{-1}) \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - (q - q^{-1})
mixed 1 -\frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \frac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1})

The (1, -(q - q^{-1})) convention for nn crossings is the unique convention consistent with the Hecke inverse relation \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - (q - q^{-1}). This is not a normalization choice — any other coefficients break \sigma \cdot \sigma^{-1} = 1 in the standard (2,1) representation. The unimodularity \det T = -1 is a theorem (consequence of the Hecke relation \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1, which forces eigenvalues q, -q^{-1} with product -1), not an assumption.

The transfer matrix at each crossing:

  T_j(q) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c_j(q - q^{-1}) + d_j & c_j \\
    c_j & d_j
  \end{pmatrix}
   \in  \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[\tfrac12][q^{\pm 1}])

has entries that are Laurent polynomials in q with exponents in [-1, 1]. The product of k_i = A - i - 1 such matrices at generator \sigma_i:

  M_i(q) =  \prod_{j=i+1}^{A-1} T_j(q)
   \in  \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[\tfrac12][q^{\pm 1}])

has entries that are Laurent polynomials in q with exponents in [-k_i, k_i]. The traced volume:

  \hat{V}_i(q) =  z(q) \cdot (M_i)_{11}(q) + (M_i)_{21}(q)

is, with z = q^3/(q^2+1),

  \hat{V}_i(q) = \frac{q^3 (M_i)_{11}(q) + (q^2+1)(M_i)_{21}(q)}{q^2+1},

a quotient of a Laurent polynomial with exponents in [-k_i, k_i + 3] by q^2 + 1. The denominator does not cancel in general (for one \mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p} crossing, \hat{V}_0 = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)).

The product P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) is therefore a rational function whose denominator divides (q^2+1)^{A-1}, and the span of its numerator is bounded by:

  \operatorname{span} N_{\mathcal{N}}
   \leq 
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} (2k_i + 3)
  = 
  2 \cdot \frac{A(A-1)}{2} + 3(A-1)
  = 
  (A-1)(A+3).

The bound is attained: a symbolic check over random crossing sequences for A \le 5 reaches it and never exceeds it.

The computation requires exactly \sum_i k_i = \binom{A}{2} transfer matrix multiplications (one per nucleon pair). No polynomial expansion occurs — the factored form is never unfolded. \square

The triple identity of q.

The parameter q plays three roles simultaneously:

Role Description
Algebraic Deformation parameter of H_A(q): T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1
Topological Variable of the Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)
Physical Substrate parameter q from \chi(A) = -6

These are not three different objects — they are the same q. The Hecke relation generates the polynomial; the Markov trace makes it a link invariant; evaluating at q projects the topological invariant to the physical energy.

Degree bounds for specific nuclei.

Nucleus A \binom{A}{2} steps \operatorname{span} N_{\mathcal{N}} \leq
{}^{2}\mathrm{H} 2 1 5
{}^{3}\mathrm{H} 3 3 12
{}^{4}\mathrm{He} 4 6 21
{}^{14}\mathrm{C} 14 91 221
{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe} 56 1540 3245
{}^{210}\mathrm{Bi} 210 21945 44517

Until 2026-10-10 this proof used the excised convention-C parameter z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}), which cancels against the numerator and gives a polynomial in q^{1/2} of degree \leq A^2 - 1 (table values 3, 8, 15, 195, 3135, 44099).

All evaluated in milliseconds.

Consequence for beta decay.

The Q-value (transition energy) is the ratio of two Skein polynomials evaluated at the substrate parameter q:

  Q
  = 
  P_{\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{par}}}(q)
  - 
  P_{\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{dau}}}(q)
  - 
  P_{e}(q)

(in action units). Since the parent and daughter polynomials differ only at generators \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_p (the 1-jet support of the beta decay (jet expansion)), the difference is a polynomial of lower degree — concentrated in the converting nucleon's generators.

Consequence for double beta decay.

The 2-jet cross-term \Delta_{p_1 p_2} (generator volume decomposition) corresponds to the interference between two Skein polynomial modifications. In the polynomial language:

  P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(2\beta)}(q)
  - 
  P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)
   \neq 
  \bigl[P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\beta_1)}(q) - P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)\bigr]
  + 
  \bigl[P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\beta_2)}(q) - P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)\bigr]

The difference is the 2-jet cross-term: a polynomial in q encoding the nuclear matrix element of double beta decay.
